title: The Open-Strategy Dictator Game: Cooperation Under Mutual Transparency
abstract: arXiv:2608.14913v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We introduce the Open-Strategy Dictator Game (OSDG), a variant of the classic dictator game in which each player's strategy is a natural-language document visible to all participants. The dictator's decision, to SHARE or TAKE an endowment, may depend on the text of the recipient's strategy. A large language model adjudicates each interaction by interpreting the dictator's strategy in the context of the recipient's. We run round-robin tournaments among diverse strategies and analyze the resulting payoff matrix using softmax equilibrium frequencies, dominance analysis, and sensitivity to the relative value of cooperation. Conditionally cooperative strategies, those that share with cooperators and take from exploiters, consistently dominate, while unconditional strategies (always share or always take) are weakly dominated. translated_title: 开放策略独裁者博弈：相互透明下的合作
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.14913v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：我们引入了开放策略独裁者博弈（OSDG），这是经典独裁者博弈的一种变体，其中每个玩家的策略是一份对所有参与者可见的自然语言文档。独裁者的决定，即分享（SHARE）或拿走（TAKE）一笔 endowment（捐赠），可能取决于接收者策略的文本内容。一个大型语言模型通过解释独裁者策略在接收者策略语境中的含义来裁决每次互动。我们进行了多种策略之间的循环锦标赛，并使用 softmax 均衡频率、优势分析和合作相对价值的敏感性分析来解析所得收益矩阵。条件合作策略——即与合作者分享、对剥削者采取拿走的策略——持续占据主导地位，而无条件策略（总是分享或总是拿走）则被弱主导。结果表明，在智能体可以相互检查决策程序的环境中，条件合作会占优。
tldr: 本文提出开放策略独裁者博弈，通过大型语言模型裁决策略互动，发现条件合作策略在相互透明的环境中持续占优，而无条件策略则被弱主导。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the Open-Strategy Dictator Game, where a large language model adjudicates strategy interactions, showing that conditionally cooperative strategies consistently dominate under mutual transparency, while unconditional strategies are weakly dominated.
